issues.legal_issue: A claimant seeking possession on the strength of title must prove that title, and failure by the opposing party to prove its own title does not by itself entitle the claimant to relief.
material_facts: The suit sought recovery of possession on the strength of a claimed title derived from a lease.
The opposing occupants denied the claimed title and asserted title of their own.
The courts below found that the claimant had not established title, while also finding that the occupants had not established the title they asserted.
issues.conclusion: The burden remained on the claimant to establish title; weakness in the defence or failure to establish the defence title could not alone support a decree for possession.
issues.legal_principle: In a suit for recovery of possession on the strength of title, the claimant must establish that title. A court may consider the rival title asserted by the defendants, but their failure to prove it does not discharge the claimant’s burden. No statutory provision or earlier case is cited for this proposition in the judgment.

predicates.possession_suit_based_on_title: The proceeding is a suit seeking possession on the basis of a claimed title.
predicates.claimant_seeks_possession: The claimant asks the court to recover possession from the opposing occupants.
predicates.opposing_title_is_unproved: The opposing occupants fail to establish the title they assert.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks possession on the basis of title and the opposing occupants do not prove their asserted title, the claimant still has to prove the claimed title.

issues.legal_issue: A belated amendment that makes the dispute more precise and assists its adjudication may be allowed when the delay can be compensated by costs.
material_facts: The claimant sought a further amendment to make the disputed property more precisely identifiable.
The amendment was sought belatedly but would help the court determine the real dispute more satisfactorily.
The court considered that the delay could be compensated by awarding costs to the opposing occupants.
issues.conclusion: The amendment was allowed, with the claimant required to pay costs thrown away and the opposing occupants permitted to respond to the amended pleading.
issues.legal_principle: The court may allow a belated amendment that enables a more precise determination of the real dispute, where the prejudice from delay can be compensated by costs. No statutory provision or earlier case is cited for this ruling in the judgment.

rule.if: civil_property_suit and amendment_sought and amendment_clarifies_real_dispute and delay_compensable_by_costs

predicates.civil_property_suit: The proceeding is a civil suit concerning rights in property.
predicates.amendment_sought: A party asks to amend its pleading.
predicates.amendment_clarifies_real_dispute: The proposed amendment makes the dispute more precise and assists its adjudication.
predicates.delay_compensable_by_costs: The prejudice caused by the lateness of the amendment can be compensated by costs.

issues.definition: When an amendment in a civil property suit clarifies the real dispute and the effects of delay can be compensated, the amendment may be allowed with costs.

issues.legal_issue: A party relying on an ancient document should have an opportunity to establish the basis for admitting a certified copy as secondary evidence when the original’s availability has not been investigated.
material_facts: The claimant relied on an old lease as the source of the claimed title but did not produce the original.
The claimant belatedly sought to rely on a certified copy, which the trial court excluded for lack of a foundation for secondary evidence.
The courts had not established whether the original document was available or given the claimant an opportunity to lay the necessary foundation.
issues.conclusion: The claimant had to be given an opportunity to produce the original lease or to adduce evidence supporting admission of the certified copy as secondary evidence; admission of the copy was not ordered automatically.
issues.legal_principle: Where an ancient document is relied on to establish title, the court should investigate the availability of the original and give the party an opportunity to lay the foundation for secondary evidence before refusing to consider a certified copy on that ground. No statutory provision or earlier case is cited for this ruling in the judgment.

rule.if: title_suit_relies_on_old_document and original_not_produced and original_availability_unexamined and certified_copy_offered

predicates.title_suit_relies_on_old_document: A party in a title suit relies on an old document as evidence of title.
predicates.original_not_produced: The party has not produced the original document.
predicates.original_availability_unexamined: The court has not investigated whether the original document is available.
predicates.certified_copy_offered: The party offers a certified copy of the document.

issues.definition: When a title claim relies on an old document whose original was not produced and whose availability has not been examined, a party offering a certified copy must have an opportunity to establish the basis for secondary evidence.

issues.legal_issue: Title to property cannot be determined from survey records alone, and the property covered by a title document may need to be identified through further evidence or a commission.
material_facts: The claimant relied on revenue records, maps, records of rights, and other documents indicating that the claimed property was held under a lease.
The appellate court placed undue reliance on City Survey records recording the occupants or their predecessor as occupants.
The dispute required determining whether the property occupied by the defendants was included in the area covered by the lease.
issues.conclusion: The title evidence had to be independently assessed rather than resolved from survey records alone, and a commission could be issued if necessary to identify the leased property and demarcate the disputed portion.
issues.legal_principle: Survey records alone do not decide title. Relevant survey records, maps, records of rights, other documents, pleadings, and oral evidence must be assessed; a commission may be used where necessary to identify the property covered by a title document. No statutory provision or earlier case is cited for this ruling in the judgment.

predicates.property_title_dispute: The proceeding involves a dispute over title to property.
predicates.survey_records_are_relied_on: A party or court relies on survey records in addressing the property dispute.
predicates.other_title_evidence_is_relevant: Other documents, maps, records, or oral evidence bear on title or the identity of the property.

issues.definition: In a property title dispute involving survey records and other relevant evidence, title must be assessed from all relevant evidence, with further identification of the property if needed.

issues.legal_issue: A matter should be remanded for a fresh trial when errors in handling pleadings and title evidence have left material questions of title and property identification unresolved.
material_facts: The trial court refused the proposed amendment and excluded the certified copy of the old lease without first giving the claimant an opportunity to establish the relevant foundation.
The appellate court did not properly assess the claimant’s documentary evidence and placed undue reliance on City Survey records.
Whether the disputed property fell within the lease and whether it could be identified required further consideration and potentially a commission.
issues.conclusion: The judgments and decrees below were set aside and the suit was remanded for a fresh trial and disposal, with the specified opportunities to amend the pleading, address the lease evidence, and identify the property.
issues.legal_principle: A fresh trial is appropriate where errors in procedure and evaluation of evidence have prevented a satisfactory determination of the real dispute and material questions remain unresolved. No statutory provision or earlier case is cited for this disposition in the judgment.

predicates.appeal_from_dismissal_of_property_suit: The proceeding is an appeal from the dismissal of a suit concerning property.
predicates.material_title_questions_unresolved: Material questions about title or the identity of the property remain undecided.
predicates.procedural_errors_prevented_satisfactory: Errors in handling pleadings or evidence prevented a satisfactory adjudication of the dispute.

issues.definition: When an appeal from dismissal of a property suit reveals unresolved material title questions because procedural errors prevented satisfactory adjudication, the matter is remanded for a fresh trial.

issues.legal_issue: The rejection of a counterclaim remains in force when the party challenging that rejection abandons its cross-objection.
material_facts: The occupants had filed a counterclaim in the trial court.
The trial court rejected the counterclaim.
The occupants filed a cross-objection challenging that rejection but did not pursue it.
issues.conclusion: The rejection of the counterclaim was confirmed and did not require reconsideration at the fresh trial.
issues.legal_principle: When a party does not pursue its cross-objection challenging rejection of a counterclaim, the rejection stands. No statutory provision or earlier case is cited for this ruling in the judgment.

predicates.appeal_includes_cross_objection_against_: The proceeding includes a cross-objection challenging the rejection of a counterclaim.
predicates.challenging_party_abandons_cross_objecti: The party that filed the cross-objection does not pursue it.

issues.definition: When a party abandons a cross-objection against rejection of a counterclaim, that rejection remains in force.
